chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord. So he remained three days not answering them, then it was revealed 'Say: He is Allah the One' to its end.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah the One

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Surah Al-Ikhlas being revealed in response to the Jews' question about God's lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Jewish inquiry into the genealogy (nasab) of Allah, a concept rooted in their anthropomorphic understanding of divinity, to which the Prophet (SAW) responded with a divine pause before the revelation of Surah Al-Ikhlas. Scholarly tradition interprets this as a definitive refutation of attributing lineage or physical form to God, establishing the core Shia doctrine of Tawhid al-Zati (Absolute Unity of Essence). The revelation serves as a concise theological manifesto, countering polytheistic and anthropomorphic views by affirming Allah's self-sufficiency and uniqueness.
